newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

EL SALVADOR, Nov 11 - Acajutla - 11 vessels due (containers, steel products, lube oil, wax, vegetable oil, general cargo, rice, vehicles), delays depend on weather , 2 vessels discharging at berth (fertiliser and rice).

MEXICO, Nov 12 - Tampico - vessels in port - 4 general cargo, 1 mineral, 1 sugar, 1 steel sheets, 1 clinker, 1 fuel. Altamira - vessels in port - 1 under repairs. Veracruz - vessels in port - 1 cars, 5 grain, 1 under repairs, 1 sugar, 2 containers, 3 corn, 1 chemicals, 1 scrap. Manzanillo - vessels in port - 3 general cargo, 3 containers, 1 cars, 1 sulphur, 1 cattle. Coatzacoalcos - vessels in port - 9 chemicals, 9 oil tankers. All ports working normally.

PANAMA, Nov 10 - Panama Canal - work on Gatun locks scheduled to complete by 2359 hours 10/11, and at Miraflores by 0600 hours 11/11, vessels awaiting transit - 62 vessels at 0001 10/11, 63 at 01 11/11, 65 at 0001 12/11, delays for vessels - 3 days for 91 ft. beam and over, and/or restricted due to cargo/draft, 2 days for under 91 ft. beam. It is estimated that traffic will return to normal levels beginning of week 46, depending on arrivals and how canal authorities are able to maintain transit schedules. The booking system remains at condition 2 (reduced slots), until further notice.

Nov 11 - Balboa - vessels in port - 2 tankers, 1 bulker. Cristobal - two general cargo vessels in port. Panama Canal - canal resumed full capacity at 0600 hours 11/11. However, delays of up to 36 hours (due to reduced capacity between 5/11 and 11/11). Based on present and projected vessel waiting times, the number of bookings allocated remains reduced until further notice. 39 vessels due, 65 in queue, 10 booked, 41 scheduled. Average waiting time for booked and non-booked vessels is 35.3 hours. Very heavy rain.

UNITED STATES, Nov 11 - Honolulu, HI - harbour - vessels alongside - 2 containers, 5 tugs and barges, 1 tanker discharging jet fuel, anchorage - 1 vessel for medical crew, 1 tanker anchored awaiting berth, 1 vessel anchored for bunkers/repairs. Barbers Point - Harbour - 1 tanker alongside loading naphtha, 1 tug and barges alongside, offport moorings - 2 tankers discharging crude.

Baltimore, MD - vessels operating - 7 bulkers, 4 container vessels, 3 ro/ro, 1 auto vessel, 2 tankers, 2 general cargo, 2 cable vessels on standby, 3 vessels in repair yard, 6 bulkers awaiting berth of which 2 to load coal, 1 to discharge coke, 1 to discharge sugar, 2 others.

Jersey City, NJ - two vessels in port. Port Newark, NJ - three vessels in port. Port Elizabeth, NJ - four vessels in port. Perth Amboy, NJ - no vessels in port. Bayview, NJ - one vessel in port. Cartaret, NJ - two vessels in port.
Hampton Roads, VA - three general cargo/container vessels in pier operating, 1 vessel in pier loading coal, 1 anchored waiting to load, 1 parcel tanker discharging, 4 vessels in pier under repairs.

East Coast - Baltimore, MD - no congestion expected at Dundalk terminal. No adverse at c,d canal/baltimore harbour low ceiling. Elevators and coal operations working well with no delays. Average waiting time consol coal 4 days. Liquid bulk facilities operating normally, no berthing congestion. Anchorage clear at Baltimore and Annapolis.

Charleston, SC - no vessels due at Shipyard River coal terminal or the grain elevator, no delays expected at tanker terminals, all terminals working well. Vessels due by 14/11. Columbus Street and Wando will be light. Some berth congestion expected at North Charleston Terminal. No navigational problems in the harbour.

Jacksonville, FL - no heavy berth congestion or delays at the port and Fernandina Beach, FL. Miami, FL - no congestion at container berths, gantry and ro/ro berths available all week. Passenger terminals in full operation.
New York, NY - no congestion at anchorages, container, tanker terminals, congestion continues at sugar terminals.

Norfolk, VA - 11 vessels due at Norfolk Southern coal pier during week, 2 vessels anchored waiting to load, 9 vessels due at Dominion terminal, 4 vessels due at Pier IX coal terminal during the week, 1 vessels due at Cargill, container and general cargo terminals working normally, no delays, oil and bulk terminals working normally, all channels are opening with prevailing depths available.

Philadelphia, PA - no congestion in ports of Philadelphia, Camden, Wilmington, no dredging/repairs/navigational problems. From 7/11 to 24/12 there will be a lighted crane barge and material barge moored to the tower pier on the Philadelphia side of the main channel. Mariners are urged to use caution while transiting the area.

Savannah, GA - moderate to heavy congestion expected at the Georgia Ports Authorities Garden City terminals for the week. Ocean terminal expecting heavy congestion midweek. All liquid bulk facilities operating normally, no berth congestion expected, no delays for bulk clay, some delays due to fog, all navigational problems remain normal.

Gulf Coast - Houston, TX - no congestion at city docks, Galveston grain elevators, congestion in oil/chemical terminals. Mobile, AL - all terminals working normally, maintenance dredging of Mobile ship channel commenced on 8/11 and expected to be ongoing for the next several months.

New Orleans, LA - rain causes delays for grain loading. Grain shipments normal for season. River stage at 4-8 ft. On Saturday and Sunday the draft for the Mississippi River gulf outlet will be 30 ft max. Permissible draft at SW pass is 47 ft fw. For vessels under 100,000 dwt, 46 ft. Fw for vessels over 100,000 dwt.

West Coast - Columbia River - Bar pilots initiating night time boardings next week using the new helicopter system as compared to traditional pilot board boarding. Coos Bay - one nickel ore discharging at Glenbrook dock, 1 vessel discharging logs at ocean terminals, 1 woodchip carrier loading at export services.

Honolulu, HI - several vessels approaching Hawaii from Guam and Japan have been delayed due to very bad weather caused by numerous typhoons in the western Pacific. Long Beach, CA - Metropolitan - moderate for month of Nov, 1-2 days berthing delay at anchor expected.

Koch Carbon - 1 vessel due in Nov. Kaiser - moderate for month of Nov, 1-2 days berthing delay for coal/petcoke. Moderate in the Los Angeles/Long Beach Harbour for bulk cargoes. Busy in December for bulk cargoes.

San Francisco, CA - the cleanup from an oil spill in San Francisco drydock is now complete. No shipping traffic was affected by the spill with the exception of the sea river vessels that conduct lightering operations in anchorage no. 9, San Francisco Bay. Fog can cause delays in vessel traffic.
